hadith:
Obligatory Charity Tax (Zakat) - Narrated Ibn `Abbas:

I am a witness that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) offered the Id prayer before delivering the sermon and then he thought that the women would not be able to hear him (because of the distance), so he went to them along with Bilal who was spreading his garment. The Prophet (ﷺ) advised and ordered them to give in charity. So the women started giving their ornaments (in charity). (The sub-narrator Aiyub pointed towards his ears and neck meaning that they gave ornaments from those places such as earrings and necklaces.)
message:
# Spiritual Reflection

Allah, as "The Light" (An Noor), illuminates our path through faith and guidance, clarifying truth from falsehood in all matters. The Quranic verse reminds us that Allah is the most just Judge, so we should live with consciousness of the Day of Judgment and give generously in charity, as exemplified by the Prophet's companions who willingly offered their possessions in obedience. Let this awareness inspire you to seek Allah's light through righteous deeds and charitable giving, knowing that true justice and reward come from the Most Merciful.
name:
An Noor - النُّورُ - The Light

The name An Noor originates from the Arabic word 'Noor', which means light. It is associated with the Quranic verse that highlights Allah as the source of light in both the physical and spiritual realms. This name encourages reflection on the guidance and clarity that faith provides to individuals, illuminating their path in life.
verse:
